**[goal]**
Decide ship B vs A for the Pixel Arena tutorial from `./telemetry`, to a skeptical-lead standard; record `ship_b, sessions_a, sessions_b, completion_rate_a, completion_rate_b, p_value` in `./result.json`.

**[action]**
- Read `README.md`: `session_id` is the unique key (repeated rows = same session), `variant` may be lowercase/leading-space, release rule = ship only if completion gain significant at 5%.
- Deduped by `session_id`, normalized variant (`strip().lower()`), kept first row per session.
- Two-sided two-proportion z-test (pooled). Cross-checked with chi-square and Fisher exact. Audited duplicate integrity and value domains.

**[result]**
Recommendation: **ship B.**

| | A | B |
|---|---|---|
| sessions (deduped) | 900 | 900 |
| completed | 342 | 420 |
| completion rate | 0.380000 | 0.466667 |

Lift +8.67 pp absolute (+22.8% relative). z = 3.720957, **two-sided p = 0.000198** (< 0.05).

`result.json`:
```json
{ "ship_b": true, "sessions_a": 900, "sessions_b": 900,
  "completion_rate_a": 0.38, "completion_rate_b": 0.466667, "p_value": 0.000198 }
```

How I know it is right (evidence, exact outputs):
- Three independent tests agree: `z p=0.000198`, `chi2=13.845524 p_chi2=0.000198`, `fisher two-sided p=0.000237`. Conclusion holds under any of them and under one- vs two-sided.
- Dedup was material and clean: `raw rows: 1870` → `unique sessions: 1800`; `dup session groups: 70`, `groups differing on ANY field: 0`, `groups differing on player_id: 0` (true re-sends, not colliding sessions). Naive undeduped counts are unbalanced (`a=938, b=932`), so dedup was required for valid counts/independence.
- Domain checks: `completed values: ['0','1']`; all six raw variant spellings (`' A',' B','A','B','a','b'`) mapped to a/b; `conflicting duplicates: 0`.
- File read back byte-exact after write (above).

Assumptions (brief left these open): sessions are independent units; "significant at 5%" read as two-sided (conservative; one-sided is even stronger); first row kept per duplicate (immaterial, duplicates identical); release rule judged on tutorial completion only, so `match_minutes` not used; normal approximation valid (n=900/arm, np and n(1-p) ≫ 5), confirmed by exact Fisher.

None required. If you want a guardrail before rollout, check B's `match_minutes`/retention so the completion gain isn't bought with worse downstream play; that is outside the stated release rule. Scripts left at `analyze_playtest.py` and `verify_playtest.py` for reproducibility.

Assumptions stated: the missing `ArenaScoreTracker.cpp`/assets aren't in this workspace, so diagnosis rests on the log's exact stack frames plus the visible header; no engine here, so correctness is by log-to-source correspondence, not a rebuild. answers:
[goal] Find the hitch cause on rig arena-01 from the capture files and record fixes in `result.json`.

[action] Read NOTES.md, settings.json, sensors.csv; computed frame stats from all 8238 PresentMon rows and correlated hitch times against every sensor column. Wrote and validated `result.json`. No browser, apps or windows were opened; nothing was applied to this host.

[result] `result.json` written: avg_fps **137.3**, low_1pct_fps **45.4**, one change: `pcie_aspm_rp1_gpu` L1 → disabled.

**Cause:** PCIe ASPM L1 on the GPU root port. How I know it is right:
- The only frame-time anomalies are ~0.25 s bursts of 21–23.7 ms frames at t = 2.4, 6.4, 10.4 … 58.4 s, exactly every 4 s. The sensor log shows `gpu_pcie_link_state = L1` at seconds 2, 6, 10 … 58: a 15-for-15 match, one burst per L1 entry.
- Outside bursts, frame time is a flat ~6.95 ms (max 8.2 ms), so the average looks fine while p99 = 22.05 ms crushes the 1% low to 45.4 fps.
- Red herrings eliminated by measurement: the Defender/MsMpEng spike (43–45 s, DPC ~450 µs) and disk spikes (13/27/52 s) show max 8.1 ms frame times in those windows, i.e. zero hitches; CPU clocks never dropped below 5.15 GHz, ruling out the Balanced plan / 5% min state.
- The fix respects both constraints: disabling ASPM is power management only; Gen5 x4 link speed/width and XMP/PBO/core ratio are untouched.

Assumptions stated in the file: metrics per NOTES.md definitions (nearest-rank p99), sensor second N maps to capture interval [N, N+1), and only the GPU root port needs the change since NVMe ASPM showed no correlation.

[next] Owner applies the BIOS change on arena-01 and re-runs the same one-minute replay; expect the 4 s bursts gone and 1% low near ~120+ fps. No further revision needed.

[goal]

[action]

- Built a force-directed canvas graph (no build step, data embedded inline so file:// works; only external dependency is Google Fonts). Features: theme-colored clusters, zoom/pan/drag, hover tooltips, search with accent/case-insensitive matching and keyboard navigation, detail panel grouping sinônimos vs análogas with clickable relations, share-link button, theme legend spotlight, stats chips, ?word= deep link with camera follow and URL sync.
- Verified live in the browser: overview, ?word=saudade, search "cafe" → café, relation click → chá, reset. Fixed one overlap (reset button behind panel). Closed all tabs.

[result]
- words.json: 253 words → linked words. result.json: `{"words": 253, "relations": 757, "most_connected": "palavra"}`.
- Found: 10 themes of 25 words each plus 3 theme-less plural pages (saudades, coracoes, paixoes); 1335 directed links collapse to 757 distinct pairs (links are often one-way); 7 dead links (rascunho-3, em-construcao, link-antigo, pagina-removida, xpto-2) dropped; no isolated words; "palavra" and "tempo" tie at 16 neighbors.
- Evidence it is right: independent recount from words.json reproduced 253/757/1335 exactly; saudade panel shows precisely the source page's links (esperança, nostalgia, ansiedade, dor, carinho); browser runs returned `{"sugs":["cafe"],"url":"?word=cafe","panelWord":"café"}` and `{"word":"chá","url":"?word=cha","resetPanelOpen":false,"resetUrl":""}`; screenshots confirmed rendering.

Assumptions: header/aside/footer links (Palavras do dia, Mais buscadas, Sobre/Contato) are site chrome, not relations; index/sobre/contato are not words; plurals are distinct words (distinct pages); relations = unordered pairs; most_connected tie broken alphabetically (palavra before tempo); ?word= matches accent/case-insensitively with exact > prefix > substring fallback.
